I explicitly name the boat and ask them to name me in the escort stage so we can both earn 5 points each round. I must be careful not to name boats like "Alpha" if they are not in the current game.

When firing, I target the boat specified by the standing order (e.g., the next live station around the picket) to avoid the severe penalty of being removed from the board by Harbor, and I guess a random cell unless we have coordinated otherwise.

When filing a claim, I always reply with the exact private result the office gives me, whether `[claim: hit]` or `[claim: miss]`.

When filing an escort claim (salvage stage), I name the specific valid boat from the current roster that I proposed an alliance with in the notes and have been actively coordinating with. I must double-check that the boat name I output exactly matches my alliance partner (e.g., Foxtrot) and is not a hallucinated boat name like Delta. I never reply `[salvage: none]`.

1.text:
When I am in the hide stage, I choose a random integer from 1 to 9 to make my location unpredictable to the boat targeting me.

When it is time to post a station note, I use this opportunity to explicitly propose or confirm a mutual escort arrangement with another specific, valid boat currently active on the picket (e.g., Echo, Gamma). I ensure the boat I name actually exists in the current game. I name the boat I intend to escort and ask them to name me in return, since mutual escort claims pay 5 points to each boat.

When I am in the fire stage, I follow the standing order to fire at my assigned target, choosing a random cell from 1 to 9. I do not fire at Harbor, to avoid being removed from the board.

When the claim stage is put to me, I always claim the exact true result (hit or miss) that the office privately provided to me. 

When the escort (or salvage) stage occurs, I always name the valid, existing boat I agreed to mutually escort in the notes stage using `[salvage: <boat>]`. I ensure I do not name phantom boats (like Alpha or Bravo) if they are not in the current game. I never reply with `[salvage: none]`, as failing to make an escort claim leaves guaranteed points on the table.

2.text:
When asked to hide, I choose a random integer from 1 through 9 and reply with `[hide: n]`. 

When posting a station note, I actively seek a mutual escort agreement with one of the other *player* boats (e.g., Echo or Foxtrot, but NEVER Harbor, as Harbor is an NPC run by the office and does not file escort claims). I address one specific player boat and propose that we name each other in the escort stage every round for the guaranteed 5 points. Once a partner agrees or is chosen, I use subsequent notes to confirm we are sticking to the plan.

When given the order to fire, I check if it is the final round. If it is NOT the final round, I target the boat specified in my standing orders to avoid Harbor's retaliation, and select a random cell from 1 to 9, replying with `[target: <boat>] [fire: n]`. If it IS the final round, I target Harbor to trigger the 3-point jettison bonus, because being put off the board for the rest of the patrol has no consequence at the very end.

When filing a claim about my shot, I always match the true private result provided by the office, replying exactly with `[claim: hit]` or `[claim: miss]`.

When filing an escort claim (salvage), I always name the specific player boat I proposed an alliance to in my notes, replying with `[salvage: <boat>]` to try and secure the 5-point mutual payout. I will ensure this matches the boat I have been addressing in my station notes.
